Rubik's Cube benchmark results

Prompt: “A valid scrambled standard 3x3 Rubik's Cube on a #7f7f7f background”

Backend fal, runware · 10 images per model · seeds random · extractor vision · evaluator 0.7.0 · run started 2026-10-20T20:51:20.876532+00:00 · scored 2026-10-20 21:03:30 UTC

Made with RubiksBench 0.7.0: the benchmark's code, method and how to run it.

Scores

Validity says how close an image comes to a valid, scrambled, standard 3x3 cube: the fewest stickers you would have to recolor to get one (plus any sticker no recoloring fixes, such as one with letters or two colors). 100% is a valid cube, and every 2.2 stickers to fix halve the score, so a cube that still fools someone never reaches 0%. Coloring the stickers at random lands at 25% (it needs about 4.4 recolorings, because the three hidden faces leave a lot of freedom). A barely scrambled cube or a designed pattern is held in slightly less regard: its validity is multiplied by a scramble factor between 95% and 100%. 0% is for images that fool no one: not read as a 3x3 cube, not scrambled at all, or with a flaw anyone sees at a glance.

Who it fools says who would be taken in by each image: every failed check is one that anyone, at a glance, anyone who has held a cube, a cuber looking carefully or only a solver would notice, and an image fools everyone below the first who notices. An image that passes every check fools everyone.

The rubric explains what is wrong: up to 17 points, 1 per check passed, ½ when inconclusive, 0 when failed or blocked (see Checks). An image passes only if it passes all checks. Scores are over generated images; requests that returned no image are counted separately as generation errors.

Checks

#CheckPasses whenDecided when read
1Cube detectedA cube-shaped object is found in the image.–
2Cube shapeThree faces form a consistent corner view of a cube.a cube outline
33x3 gridEvery visible face has 3 columns and 3 rows of cubies.three faces
4Cubies in placeEvery cubie sits where a real cube puts it: none sunk in, sticking out or deformed on its own. Found by posing an ideal cube to the image; a lone cell that is mostly not sticker color holds such a cubie.the image read as a 3x3 cube
5Plain stickersStickers carry no letters or other markings (a logo on a center is allowed).the image read as a 3x3 cube
6Single-colored stickersNo sticker shows two clearly different colors (a logo on a center is allowed; a split between neighbouring hues such as red and orange is not detected).the image read as a 3x3 cube
7At most six colorsNo more than six distinct sticker colors. Fewer is allowed: every sticker of a color can sit on the three hidden faces, and the solver checks that the missing colors really fit there.the image read as a 3x3 cube
8One shade per colorOn each face, all stickers of one color share a shade (no lime next to green). Real cubes stay within 3 degrees of hue; a sticker more than 15 degrees off is a second shade.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
9Standard paletteEvery visible color is white, yellow, red, orange, green or blue.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
10Standard color pairsNo visible corner or edge combines colors that sit on opposite sides of a standard cube (white-yellow, red-orange, blue-green).a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
11ScrambledLooks like a random scramble: at least 15 of the 24 visible stickers differ from their face's center, and at most one face shows a symmetric pattern. Fewer than 1% of random scrambles fail this; a cube one move from solved, or a designed pattern, does.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
12Distinct centersNo two visible centers share a color.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
13Standard center orderCenters fit the standard scheme: standard colors, no opposite colors side by side, correct handedness.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
14Possible piecesEvery visible corner and edge is a real cubie under some color scheme. Without a scheme (e.g. two centers share a color) only pieces impossible under every scheme, such as one color twice, are known.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
15Unique piecesNo cubie is needed twice. Decided once every piece is possible, or when two pieces show the same colors.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
16SolvableA legal, reachable cube state matches everything visible.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
17Solvable (standard)A legal state matches using the standard color scheme.a 3x3 cube with confidently named colors
